speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To understand the severity and location of your symptoms, can you tell me exactly which arm is affected and whether the weakness makes it difficult to grip objects?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy (CSM).

Based on your history of long-standing neck/arm pain, paresthesias, progressive bilateral hand weakness, and age-related risk factors, the clinical picture strongly suggests cervical spine stenosis compressing the spinal cord. I am requesting an MRI of the Cervical Spine to confirm this diagnosis and assess the severity of cord compression.
